We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse structure: It's a tolyl (para methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring which is para-substituted with an α,β-unsaturated amide (trans). The amide is attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) i.e., an aniline with an extra NH? Actually C(=O)N attached to phenyl with an NH at para? The SMILES: ...C(=O)N c3ccccc3N . So amide attached to an aniline (anilide) with an extra NH on the phenyl (maybe an aniline). So overall three steps: 1) formation of sulfonamide between tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the second phenyl with sulfonyl attached). 2) formation of amide via coupling of carboxylic acid (from Doebner product) with aniline (the aniline with NH). 3) formation of α,β-unsaturated acid via Doebner modification from aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between carbonyl carbon and aniline nitrogen (step 1). Precursors: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (aryl-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then disconnect the C=C double bond formation via Doebner: precursor aldehyde (aryl-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde is the phenyl ring attached to sulfonyl group? Actually the α,β-unsaturated acid is attached to phenyl ring that also bears sulfonyl group (connected to tolyl). So aldehyde precursor is that phenyl ring with sulfonyl group and aldehyde para to sulfonyl? In target, the unsaturated chain is attached to phenyl at para position relative to sulfonyl? SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to sulfonyl. So phenyl ring (ring2) has sulfonyl at position 1, and the unsaturated chain at para (position 4). So aldehyde precursor would be same phenyl ring with sulfonyl and aldehyde at para: c2ccc(C=O)cc2 with sulfonyl attached. So step 2: sulfonamide formation between tolyl sulfonyl chloride and aniline (the phenyl ring with aldehyde). Actually sulfonamide is between tolyl sulfonyl chloride (p-tolyl-SO2Cl) and the phenyl ring (the second phenyl) which has an amine? Wait target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to tolyl (p-tolyl) and to phenyl ring (the second). So the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl sulfonyl and to phenyl ring (the second). So the phenyl ring is attached via its nitrogen (i.e., an aniline) to the sulfonyl. So the phenyl ring must have an amine (NH) that reacts with sulfonyl chloride. In target, that nitrogen is part of sulfonamide, not part of amide. So the phenyl ring (ring2) has an NH attached to sulfonyl, and also the unsaturated chain attached to the ring (para). So the phenyl ring is an aniline (NH) that is sulfonylated. So retrosynthesis: disconnect sulfonamide bond to give p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride (or p-tolyl sulfonyl fluoride) and the aniline (ring2) bearing aldehyde (or later unsaturated acid). So step 3: sulfonyl chloride formation from p-tolyl sulfonic acid? But we can assume commercially available p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus three steps: 1) amide coupling (carboxylic acid + aniline). 2) Doebner condensation (aldehyde + malonic acid). 3) sulfonamide formation (p-tolyl sulfonyl chloride + aniline). That matches guidance.

Now need to produce JSON route with reactions and template IDs. We need to find appropriate template IDs for each transformation. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with functional groups broken/formed.

First, amide coupling: forward reaction: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide, breaking aliphatic carboxylic acid, forming amide. Use functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines? The amine is aromatic amine (aniline) which is primary amine. So broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, primary amines. Formed: amide. Let's search.
